items.title: Why Dominion Energy Halted Dividend Growth Despite Strong Operating Performance
items.summary: Dominion Energy has kept its quarterly payout frozen for years while pouring billions into offshore wind and data center infrastructure, and now a pending merger with NextEra is forcing retirees to decide whether patience will finally be rewarded or replaced by a 5% Treasury yield.

items.title: VST Keeps Writing Checks To Its Shareholders
items.summary: This power generator sent billions back to its owners. But with its stock falling and key markets in flux, shareholders are now asking what that money truly bought.

items.title: Bond Market Collapse Sends Yields to Decades-Old Highs. Dividend Stocks Are Most at Risk.
items.summary: Treasury yields just hit levels not seen in two decades, and that quiet shift is forcing income investors to ask a question they haven't had to seriously consider in years: why own dividend stocks at all?

items.title: GE Vernova vs. Duke Energy: Which Power Stock Is a Better Pick Today?
items.summary: GEV and DUK are positioned to benefit from rising electricity demand, with growth driven by power generation, grid investment and data centers.

items.title: 4 Utility Stocks With Reliable Dividends and a Massive New Growth Engine
items.summary: Data centers are quietly reshaping which utility stocks deserve a spot in an income portfolio, and four regulated electric companies just locked in contracts that could rewrite their dividend growth stories for the next decade.

items.title: NextEra Energy vs. Duke Energy: Which Utility Stock Looks Stronger?
items.summary: DUK stands out with a cheaper valuation, higher dividend yield and slightly lower debt, while NEE leads on ROIC.

items.title: Southern Company or Duke Energy: Only One Offers the Combination of Yield, Growth, and Safety You Need
items.summary: Duke Energy and Southern Company both serve regulated Southern markets, both raise their dividends annually, and both benefit from surging data center demand, but a close look at their balance sheets and capital plans reveals a clear winner for retirement income portfolios.
